title: Planar and Three-Dimensional Printing of Conductive Inks
protocol: Dissolve poly(acrylic acid) blend in a mixture of water and diethanolamine.
Inject aqueous silver nitrate solution into the polymer solution.
Obtain a light yellow transparent solution after addition.
Stir the solution for 24 hours at room temperature.
Sonicate the solution at 65 °C in a water bath for 2 hours.
Transfer the sonicated solution to a 500 ml beaker and cool it to room temperature.
Titrate 300 ml of ethanol into the solution at a rate of 30 ml/min.
Centrifuge the precipitate collected after decanting supernatant at 9000 rpm for 20 minutes.
Add a humectant solution, such as ethylene glycol, to the ink.
Homogenize the mixture at 2000 rpm for 3 minutes using a Thinky homogenization mixer.
Load ink into a syringe barrel.
Attach a deposition nozzle to the syringe barrel.
Mount the ink-loaded syringe onto the 3-axis printing stage.
Adjust the nozzle height with a telescope lens at 10x zoom.
Apply pressure using an air-powered fluid dispensing system.
Deposit ink onto the substrate with controlled printing speed.
Print silver microelectrodes in various layouts and sizes.
Pattern conductive silver grids with center-to-center line spacing of 100 μm on silicon wafers.
Create high aspect ratio cylindrical structures by layer-by-layer printing method.
Print silver microelectrodes between two glass substrates offset by a 1-mm height difference.
